chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There used to be for Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) cushions and patterns with images therein. He used to sit upon these.
ai.seo_question: Did the Imams use cushions with images?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights that Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) possessed cushions and rugs featuring images (tamathil), which he used for sitting, thereby providing a key textual basis for the permissibility of images in non-worship contexts. In Shia jurisprudence, this narration is often cited to distinguish between images intended for veneration or idolatry and those used for general adornment or utility, supporting the view that not all depictions are inherently prohibited. The presence of such items in the household of the Imams underscores the practical application of image usage in daily life, provided they do not lead to shirk.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There used to be for Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, cushions and patterns with images therein. He<sup>asws</sup> used to sit upon these’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih al-Sindiy from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, (in his house) had pillows and floor furnishings which had pictures (of sceneries) on which he (the Imam) sat.’”
